This is already fascinating. 📆 Estreno: September 25, 2026 🎭 Género: #Thriller #CrimeDrama ✈️ Add to watchlist Director Lance Oppenheim, who apparently first encountered "To Catch a Predator" through South Park parodies, has turned that secondhand mythology into an A24 thriller. That detail matters, because Primetime feels less like a biopic and more like an obsession with why Hansen became an icon in the first place. Pattinson nailed it when he said there's "something he's doing" behind that show's staying power, something you can't name even after watching thousands of hours. The camera loves certain people for reasons that defy logic. Hansen is one of them. Hansen walking out of the A24 screening over an NDA is, weirdly, very on-brand.

🍿 Supergirl hits HBO Max September 10. The discourse is already warming up. 📆 Estreno: September 10, 2026 (HBO Max) 🎭 Género: #Superhero · #SciFi · #DCU ✈️ Add to watchlist Milly Alcock is genuinely good casting. A jaded, punk-edged Kara with real bite, nothing like the blue-eyed scout of old. What drags the film down is everything around her: the script, the palette, that oppressive murky brown and yellow grade that makes every frame look like it was shot inside a diesel engine. Director Craig Gillespie reportedly skipped Tom King and Bilquis Evely's source comic entirely before taking the job. It shows. The book's visual poetry is striking; the film's is not. Deliberately ignoring your source material isn't a bold creative choice, it's just hubris with receipts.

🍿 The Angry Birds Movie 3 rips off the Dune poster and somehow earns it 📆 Estreno: December 23, 2026 🎭 Género: #Animation · #Comedy · #Family ✈️ Add to watchlist "Lisan al Birdee." That poster is funnier than most blockbuster marketing this year. Director John Rice and Jason Sudeikis are leaning hard into self-awareness, and it works. The first The Angry Birds Movie had no business being as funny as it was. Solid jokes, real craft underneath the IP slop. Three films in, the franchise is still betting on meme culture as its engine, and honestly, that bet looks smarter every time.
